maria: Heads-up — after kernel-picker v2 rollout (~2h) p99 for host-preproc is up ~18% on prod. Short streaming requests (<128 tokens) over gRPC show increased tail. Traces point at more time in proto_unmarshal and writev coalescing. Lower effective throughput too.

sam: Can you share a quick pprof/flame and which kernel variants are now being chosen for short flows? Any change in request mix?

maria: Repro command I used: `wrk -c200 -d60 -s scripts/short-stream.lua`

Log-ish sample (top-of-stack percentages from perf sampling):
```
proto_unmarshal 36%\nkv_cache_lookup 8%\nwritev_coalesce 21%\nkernel_dispatch 4%\nother 31%\n```

maria: Notable: kernel used to be `a64-fastpath` for short seqs; after picker tweak many flows now pick `unified-quant`. That seems correlated.

raj: Ran a quick pprof on a small canary. KV hit-rate dropped 98% -> 87% for short requests when unified-quant is picked. Small frames amplify proto_unmarshal cost per-request (more frames per second). Also seeing micro GC pauses in preproc ~0.6-0.9ms occasionally.

luis: Hypothesis: changing kernel changes batching hints (sequence-length histogram shifted) so the batching window emits smaller batches, increasing per-request syscall overhead and writev fragmentation. Mitigations: 1) revert kernel-picker rule for seq<256, 2) add a proto_unmarshal fastpath for tiny frames, 3) widen writev coalesce window for gRPC smallwrites.

maria: Batcher stats snapshot (before -> after): `avg_batch_size 5 -> 2`, `avg_batch_latency 1.2ms -> 3.0ms`. Batcher log line: `batcher: hint=auto size=2 latency=3ms` vs prior `size=5 latency=1.2ms`.

sam: Could kv eviction or key shape change be spreading cache hits? Raj, can you dump some kvcache key prefixes to confirm whether unified-quant is altering keys?

raj: Sample prefixes we saw: `model:v2:unq:prefix_hash=0x1a3f`, `model:v2:fast:prefix_hash=0x1a3f` — keys are colliding but TTLs/versions differ, so effective hit distribution changed. Also captured a tiny flame snippet showing proto_unmarshal hot paths bump after picker: `preproc->frame_parse->proto_unmarshal (hot)`.

deploy-bot: Deployed kernel-picker v2 to 6 hosts in prod at 6299997600 by infra-release. Rollback available if needed.

maria: For short-term: can we revert the picker rule for small seqs and measure? Also we need a micro-optim for proto_unmarshal fastpath — even a 20% reduction there will bring p99 back.

luis: I'll prototype a branchless length-check + checksum-skip fastpath for frames <256B and run it on a canary tomorrow morning. Also proposing we emit metric `effective_batch_size_by_kernel` and `kvcache_hit_by_kernel`.

sam: I'll open a rollback PR to remove the seq<256 mapping and bump the gRPC coalesce window to 4ms for host-preproc. That should increase batch size back to ~4 and reduce syscall pressure.

maria: Awesome — tagging @sre for incident tracking. Adding a short postmortem checklist: revert picker rule, patch proto_unmarshal fastpath, add metrics, run 1h wrk regression vs baseline.

luis: Quick note — if we revert but keep unified-quant in the catalog, we should still allow an opt-in canary where we force kv-key-stable hashing to avoid kvcache spread. I'll draft a small PR for stable-prefixing.

maria: Thanks all. Will post pprof links and wrk outputs to the ticket once I finish another run. :thumbsup:
